result.reasoning:
REFUTED. The reporter's arithmetic reproduces exactly, but the output is not wrong: "median" in this engine means torch's lower median, the kernel uses it consistently, and the proposed fix would actively degrade the operator.

1. The kernel's center IS the engine's own median. `torch.nanmedian(w, dim=-1).values` at ops_ext.py:654 is byte-identical (atol=0, rtol=0) to AlphaCube's built-in `cross_med(x, d)` at every grid window d in {3,5,10,30,60,241}. That is not a coincidence: AlphaCube's shared helpers `nanmedian_last` (common.py:456-457) and `_median` (common.py:395-396) are literally `w.nanmedian(dim=-1).values`, and the built-ins `cross_med` (dt_cross.py:239), `in_med` (dt_in.py:384), `ts_med` (nd_ts.py:183) and `day_median` all route through them. So `median_d` in the docstring denotes the same median as `cross_med`, the operator a reader would actually compose this with. The suggested fix would make `cross_madz`'s center disagree with `cross_med` in 18%-61% of cells (1794/9994 at d=3 up to 6131/9996 at d=10) -- i.e. the "fix" is what would introduce an inconsistency, not remove one.

2. The suggested fix injects a degenerate signal where the kernel correctly masks. `mad > 0` is a documented guard ("NaN with ... MAD = 0", rationale: tell "standardising is the wrong idea" from "the estimator was fragile"). With an even, half-pinned window the textbook MAD is nonzero only because it averages across the pinned pair. Worst case is small n: at d=3 with exactly 2 finite days (13.1% of defined cells on a panel with 7% suspensions), textbook MAD is exactly half the gap, so z collapses to the constant +/-0.674491 -- a pure sign carrying no magnitude. On my (400,300) d=3 sweep that two-point mass dominated the ranking: top-decile overlap between kernel and the "fixed" variant was 0.035, i.e. the fix's selection is nearly disjoint from the kernel's and driven by arbitrary tie-breaks among +/-0.674. The reporter's own `[3,2,2,1]` case is the same shape (2 of 4 values pinned at the median), so that cell is not "a valid day silently dropped" -- it is the guard firing on a half-degenerate window.

3. Nothing depends on textbook-median semantics. No test (tests/test_partura.py, tests/test_steer.py) touches madz; there is no numpy/pandas cross-check of these kernels anywhere in the repo. The MAD->0 masking is already known and diagnosed in the project's own notes: handoff/TOOLING.md:115 records `cross_madz` fed a series with a point mass at 0 -> "MAD->0, cov 0.70, net -6.8%", attributed to the estimator being fed the wrong input, not to a kernel bug.

4. No research conclusion is biased. The reporter concedes causality is unaffected, which I confirmed (`rolling_windows(x, d, 0)` left-pads with NaN, so day t sees only days <= t). The convention is identical across train/valid/holdout, so selection readings stay comparable. On random returns the kernel and textbook variants' long-only top-decile excess differed only within noise and with no systematic sign (d=30 continuous: -1.81 vs -2.02 bp; d=10: -1.35 vs -1.03 bp).

What remains is purely the precision of one docstring word, which is out of scope (style/naming/comments not reported) -- and the file already warns readers at ops_ext.py:16 that the docstring is the definition, while the engine-wide meaning of "median" is fixed by `cross_med`. A docstring-only reimplementation differing in an unspecified tie-break convention is a property of any such reimplementation, not a defect in the kernel; the reporter themselves showed all 39,420 sampled cells match once the reference adopts the house convention, which isolates this as a convention difference rather than an error.

result.corrected_fix: Do not change the kernel. Changing `torch.nanmedian` to a textbook median at ops_ext.py:654-655 would (a) break agreement with the engine's own `cross_med`/`in_med`/`ts_med`/`day_median`, all of which are torch lower median via `nanmedian_last` (AlphaCube common.py:456-457), and (b) replace the `mad > 0` guard's NaN with a degenerate constant +/-0.674 wherever the window is half-pinned or n=2 (13.1% of defined d=3 cells), which on my sweep took over the top-decile ranking entirely (overlap 0.035). If anything is worth doing it is a one-clause docstring edit, not a kernel change: say "median" means the engine's `cross_med` median (the lower of the two central values at an even finite count), so `MAD_d = 0` reads as "at least half the window sits exactly at the median". The same clause would apply to in_madz (ops_ext.py:379-393) and cs_robust_z (ops_ext.py:442-446), which share the convention deliberately. Note cs_robust_z differs on a separate axis the report does not raise -- it uses an absolute EPS rather than the relative `1e-6 * |median|` of the other two -- but that is a documented design contrast, not part of this claim.
